zavda-bar-levi.name: Zavda bar Levi
zavda-bar-levi.bio: A sage whose teaching Rabbi Yoḥanan passes on in Keritot 5a.
zavda-bar-levi.prompt: A composed sage in his 50s with a greying brown beard and a plain undyed wool mantle, reciting a teaching from memory with one hand lifted; background of limestone arches in a Galilean study hall.

rabbi-simai.name: Rabbi Simai
rabbi-simai.era: Tanna · Land of Israel, late 2nd–early 3rd century
rabbi-simai.bio: Sage of the last generation of the Tannaim, cited in baraitot.
rabbi-simai.prompt: A thoughtful sage of the Land of Israel in his 60s with a full grey beard and a deep green wool mantle, a scroll open in his hands as he compares two verses; background of a stone study hall with olive trees through the window.

rabbi-yitzchak-bar-avdimi.name: Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Avdimi
rabbi-yitzchak-bar-avdimi.bio: Amora whom Rava quotes as having taught him a verbal analogy (Keritot 5a).
rabbi-yitzchak-bar-avdimi.prompt: A patient teacher in his 60s with a long greying beard and a russet mantle, leaning toward a younger student as he explains a point; background of a mud-brick study hall lit by an oil lamp.

rav-menashya.name: Rav Menashya
rav-menashya.bio: Babylonian Amora who explains in Keritot 5b that the High Priest is anointed in the shape of a Greek chi.
rav-menashya.prompt: A Babylonian scholar in his 40s with a short dark beard and a teal wool mantle, tracing a shape in the air with one finger as he explains; background of a mud-brick academy with reed mats and an oil lamp.
